key_insight: NeFTY represents the 3D thermal diffusivity as a continuous neural field and couples it with a differentiable transient heat solver to recover quantitative subsurface material properties from surface temperature measurements, addressing lateral diffusion and optimization instability in prior methods.
problem_solved: Enables accurate, quantitative 3D reconstruction of material diffusivity from transient thermography data, overcoming limitations of pixel-wise 1D approximations that ignore lateral heat flow and soft-constrained PINNs that struggle with gradient stiffness in transient diffusion problems.
method: Parameterize the spatially-varying 3D thermal diffusivity as a continuous neural field (implicit neural representation).
Integrate a differentiable forward solver for transient heat diffusion to propagate gradients from surface temperature measurements back to the neural field parameters for end-to-end inversion.
Use physics-driven losses and training/regularization strategies to stabilize optimization and produce quantitative, high-resolution reconstructions.
impact: Provides a practical differentiable-physics toolkit for inverse thermal imaging and non-destructive evaluation, enabling ML practitioners to build more accurate, physics-consistent reconstructions and to apply neural fields to PDE-constrained inverse problems.

paper_title: Neural Field Thermal Tomography: A Differentiable Physics Framework for Non-Destructive Evaluation
